question: What is another common name for first-generation antipsychotic drugs?
explanation: First-generation antipsychotics are traditionally referred to as typical antipsychotics because they were the first group developed to treat psychosis. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why are second-generation antipsychotics preferred over first-generation agents in many clinical settings?

options.A: They carry a lower risk of movement side effects
options.B: They work exclusively on serotonin receptors
options.C: They require no routine laboratory monitoring
options.D: They cure schizophrenia permanently within weeks

explanation: Second-generation drugs cause fewer extrapyramidal symptoms due to their unique balance of dopamine and serotonin blockade. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h1)

question: Which neurotransmitter receptor is primarily blocked by all antipsychotic drugs to reduce psychosis?
explanation: D2 dopamine receptor blockade in the brain is the core mechanism shared by all antipsychotic medications to control psychotic symptoms. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: Blocking dopamine receptors in the mesolimbic pathway achieves which primary therapeutic goal?

options.A: Prevention of severe allergic skin reactions
options.B: Stimulation of appetite and weight gain
options.D: Improvement of social withdrawal and apathy

explanation: The mesolimbic pathway regulates emotion and perception, so blocking dopamine there specifically targets positive symptoms like hallucinations. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: Which medication belongs to the first-generation class of antipsychotics?
explanation: Haloperidol is a high-potency conventional antipsychotic classified under first-generation agents. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h3)

question: What primary characteristic defines the mechanism of first-generation antipsychotics compared to newer agents?

options.A: Direct stimulation of GABA release in the cortex
options.B: Complete absence of neurological side effects
options.C: High potency for blocking dopamine D2 receptors
options.D: Exclusive binding affinity for serotonin receptors

explanation: First-generation drugs derive their main therapeutic and adverse effects from strong blockade of dopamine D2 receptors. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is a recognized metabolic side effect of many second-generation antipsychotics?
explanation: Second-generation antipsychotics are notorious for causing metabolic changes, prominently featuring substantial weight gain and elevated blood glucose. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h4)

question: Clozapine is unique among antipsychotics because it requires careful monitoring for which serious blood disorder?
explanation: Clozapine carries a severe risk of reducing white blood cell counts, necessitating strict leukocyte monitoring protocols. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h4)

question: A patient taking haloperidol exhibits a severe, painful spasm of the neck muscles hours after the first dose. What is this condition called?
explanation: Acute dystonia involves sudden, painful muscle contractions of the neck, jaw, or eyes, typically occurring shortly after starting typical antipsychotics. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which symptom characterizes tardive dyskinesia when it develops after long-term antipsychotic therapy?

options.A: Resting tremors accompanied by a shuffling gait
options.B: Involuntary movements of the tongue and face
options.C: Inability to sit still with constant pacing
options.D: Sudden high fever and severe muscle rigidity

explanation: Tardive dyskinesia presents as late-appearing, involuntary, repetitive movements, prominently affecting the facial muscles and tongue. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is the initial priority nursing action when a patient develops symptoms of neuroleptic malignant syndrome?

options.A: Apply warm blankets to combat shivering
options.B: Encourage oral fluids to prevent dehydration
options.D: Administer an extra dose of the medication

explanation: The single most critical step in managing NMS is the immediate discontinuation of the causative antipsychotic agent. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which clinical findings are most characteristic of neuroleptic malignant syndrome?

options.A: Severe watery diarrhea and sudden weight loss
options.B: High fever and extreme muscle rigidity
options.C: Pinpoint pupils and shallow respiratory rate
options.D: Itchy skin rash and generalized urticaria

explanation: NMS is classically recognized by the dangerous combination of hyperthermia, 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h6)

question: What standardized tool do nurses use to monitor for the development of tardive dyskinesia?
explanation: The AIMS tool is specifically designed to detect and track involuntary movements associated with tardive dyskinesia in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why is patient education regarding the gradual discontinuation of antipsychotics vital?

options.A: Abrupt stopping can trigger a return of psychotic symptoms
options.B: Sudden cessation always causes permanent muscle paralysis
options.C: Stopping abruptly will immediately cause severe hyperglycemia
options.D: Patients will forget how to take their other medications

explanation: Abruptly stopping antipsychotics risks rapid relapse and a severe rebound of psychotic symptoms, so tapering under medical supervision is necessary. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h7)
